# AudioSmith's patches to MyGo

AudioSmith builds against `third_party/mygo` (the `replace` in `go.mod`): MyGo at the version `go.mod` requires, with these patches, made by `scripts/vendor-mygo.sh` from the module cache. The copy leaves out MyGo's website, docs, examples, CI, tests and test data; `scripts/vendor-mygo.sh --check` tells whether it is exactly what the script makes. Never edit `third_party/mygo` by hand: change a patch and run the script.

Keep each patch small and send it upstream (egoist/mygo); drop it when a release has the fix. With no patch left, delete `third_party/mygo` and the replace (`go mod edit -dropreplace github.com/egoist/mygo`).

| Patch | Why |
|---|---|
| `0001-coretext-own-width.patch` | On macOS a long single-line text given exactly its measured width ended in "…", and wrapping text in a box of its own width dropped its last word to a second line: `CTTypesetterSuggestLineBreak` forgives a width at most 0.0002 DIPs short of its own, and MyGo sums a line's width in float32, which loses more on long lines. The patch sums widths in float64 and breaks at width × (1 + 1e-6). MyGo 0.5 fixed the other half of the original patch itself (`penAdvances` counts the room Core Text leaves between runs of two fonts, as in "M4B（含章节）"); on 0.5.5 without the patch, its test still fails 10 cases on macOS 26.7 (long lines, 20-point text). The patch header explains it in full. |
| `0002-select-list-scrolls.patch` | `ui.Select`'s list had no height limit and no scroll: a long one (Kokoro's 25 voices, the gallery's categories) ran off the bottom of the window, its last options out of reach. The list now scrolls in the room left below the trigger (at most 20 rows' worth); the highlighted option already scrolled into view. |
| `0003-update-prereleases.patch` | Beta channel (thread #52). GitHub's latest release, which apps updated from GitHub read, is never a prerelease, so MyGo had no way to offer a beta. `mygo.Updater.SetPrereleases(true)` makes `Check` (and so the updater plugin's window and daily checks) find the newest version among releases and prereleases through the GitHub API, skipping drafts, and read the manifest of that release; when the API fails it checks the latest release instead. `mygo build -upload` creates a prerelease version's draft with `--prerelease`, and on GitHub makes deltas from the newest prerelease's manifest as well as the latest release's. Docs and tests in the patch (the docs are left out of the copy). |
| `0004-notarize-wait-again.patch` | Releases (thread #50 follow-up). `notarytool submit --wait` failed the build when the runner lost its connection during a long wait (a new team's first notarizations took 40–50 minutes), although Apple kept processing the submission. `notarize` now takes the submission id from notarytool's progress and waits for it again (`notarytool wait`) up to 5 times, 30 s apart. Test in the patch (`TestSubmissionID`). |
| `0005-atlas-stable-repack.patch` | Reproducible snapshots (refactor batch B0, thread #57). When a glyph atlas fills up, `text.System.makeRoom` gathers the glyphs it keeps from maps and `scene.Atlas.Repack` places them again, tallest first; rectangles of one size kept that map order, so a glyph could land elsewhere in the atlas from run to run, and glyphs drawn scaled (the workflow canvas) rounded 1–3 pixels differently. `Repack` now orders rectangles of one size by their place in the atlas. Test in the patch (`TestAtlasRepackOrder`, fails without it). |
| `0006-forget-glyphs.patch` | Snapshots independent of test order (refactor batch B3a, thread #64). The glyph atlases belong to MyGo's process-wide text system, so where a glyph lands depends on everything drawn before, and a test's pictures of the zoomed workflow canvas changed by ±1 in a few pixels when a test file's new name made it run later. `ui.ForgetGlyphs()` (`text.System.ForgetGlyphs`, `scene.Atlas.ResetSize`) forgets the glyphs and masks and empties both atlases to their first size; `pinSnapshots` calls it before every snapshot test. Test in the patch (`TestForgetGlyphs`, fails without the reset). |
| `0007-updater-client-and-resume.patch` | Updates behind a proxy (user report 2026-10-16: the beta.2 → beta.3 update failed with `unexpected EOF`). The updater used `http.DefaultClient`, which reads the proxy only from environment variables (apps started from the Finder have none) and never the macOS system proxy. `Updater.SetHTTPClient` lets the app pass its own client (AudioSmith's follows Settings → Models' proxy, then the system proxy), and a download whose connection drops resumes with a Range request, up to 4 times. Test `TestDownloadResumesThroughClient`. |
| `0008-update-url-prereleases.patch` | Updates from actnow.dev (thread #69). Patch 0003's beta channel only worked on GitHub; updates from a `url` had one manifest. A URL feed now has a `beta/` directory beside it, by convention (`update.PrereleaseFeed`): with `SetPrereleases(true)`, `Check` reads both manifests and offers the newer, the releases' alone when the beta one is missing (404). `mygo build` points a prerelease's archive and deltas into `beta/` and makes deltas from both manifests; `-upload` to S3 puts a prerelease under `<prefix>/beta/`, and a release also writes its manifest there unless a newer prerelease is published. GitHub mode is unchanged. AudioSmith builds every version, beta or not, with `updates.url` = `https://actnow.dev/updates/audiosmith` (thread #71): a beta's manifest then names `…/audiosmith/beta/<archive>`, as actnow.dev's release check requires, and the app reads `beta/` only with Receive beta updates on. AudioSmith no longer uploads with MyGo (`scripts/actnow-publish.sh` sends the files through the website); the S3 part stays because the patch is meant for upstream as one piece. Tests `TestPrereleaseFeed`, `TestUpdaterURLPrereleases`, `TestWriteDeltasURLPrereleases`, `TestPublishS3`. |
| `0009-menu-shift-key-equivalent.patch` | Act's 0016 (Act @fc93dbe), unchanged. A menu accelerator with Shift and a character key ("CmdOrCtrl+Shift+P") became the key equivalent "p" with Shift in the mask: AppKit showed ⇧⌘P but matched it with ⌘P too (on mac-air Act's ⌘J ran the ⇧⌘J item, which came first in the menu bar), and ⇧⌘P as typed matched nothing, so the key went past the menu to the window. As AppKit's own menus: the character Shift types ("P"; "!" for 1, "?" for / as on a US keyboard) and no Shift in the mask; Enter, arrows and F-keys keep Shift in the mask. Menu bar and context menus. Test: `TestKeyEquivalentShift` (internal/darwin). Written as an upstream PR (its header is the PR text). Here: the Edit menu's Redo (its role's ⇧⌘Z) now takes ⇧⌘Z as Undo takes ⌘Z: the focused element gets the `redo` command, and a window shortcut for ⇧⌘Z (`c.Shortcut`) no longer sees the key, as one for ⌘Z never did (both checked on mac-air with a probe app). AudioSmith's Dub editor had only such window shortcuts (`dubShortcuts`: ⌘Z never reached it on macOS, ⇧⌘Z did); it takes the Edit menu's `undo`/`redo` commands now (`dubCommand`, `TestDubEditMenuUndoRedo`). |
| `0010-editor-wrap-shaped-widths.patch` | Studio script editor (thread #98, user report on beta.6): on the Mac the last letter or two of every row of Chinese text were cut in half at the editor's right edge. `ui/editor`'s soft wraps summed the widths of characters shaped one by one, and the rows were shaped whole to paint; Core Text shapes a Chinese comma or full stop alone half as wide as between ideographs (7.6 against 15.1 DIPs at 15 points), so rows came out 30–40 DIPs wider than the wrap width. Wraps now sum the advances the characters take in the line and shape each row they break as it paints, giving back a place to break until it fits (`fitRow`). Audiobook's manuscript uses the same editor. Tests: `TestWrappedRowsFitTheWrapWidth` (in the patch; 360 rows past the width on macOS 26 without it, none with it) and AudioSmith's `TestScriptEditorWrapsInside`. |
| `0011-editor-wrap-cache.patch` | Performance review #102, fixed in thread #105: patch 0010 shaped every line it wrapped at every layout, with no cache, and `measureWraps`' 4 ms budget did not hold (400 lines near the anchor measured without looking at the time, the others 256 at a time), so opening or resizing a long manuscript took 60–120 ms in a frame and a keystroke 1–4 ms. A cache keyed by each line's displayed text keeps its in-line advances (per style and scale) and its breaks (per wrap width), and the widths of the rows `fitRow` shaped: typing reshapes only the line typed in, another width reuses the advances, and rows shaped for painting go into the frame's layouts. `measureWraps` measures the lines that show whatever the budget, then the rest within it, looking at the time every 4 lines. 0010's correctness is unchanged (same rows; `TestWrappedRowsFitTheWrapWidth`). Tests in the patch: `TestWrapCacheFollowsEdits`, `TestMeasureWrapsKeepsItsBudget`. Numbers in the patch header. |
| `0012-magnify-gesture.patch` | Dub timeline zoom (thread #107): a touchpad pinch on macOS reached no element, so a timeline could zoom only with ⌘+scroll. The surface view's `magnifyWithEvent:` now sends `PointerMagnify` (NSEvent's `magnification`, with the modifiers), which the runtime gives as `InputMagnify` (`InputEvent.Magnify`, the factor being 1+Magnify) to the innermost element under the pointer that handles its input, as it does `InputScroll`; nothing happens when none takes it, and other platforms send none. The Tester gets `Magnify(x, y, m)` and `ScrollWith(mods, …)` (`Scroll` sends no modifiers, so tests could not drive ⌘+wheel). Test in the patch: `TestMagnify`; AudioSmith's `TestTimelineGestures`. |
| `0013-tray-dot.patch` | Menu bar dot (thread #132, user request 11-01): AudioSmith's icon is a template, which macOS tints for light and dark menu bars and which therefore cannot carry a colour, but its dot must be red while the app generates and violet while an agent is connected over MCP. `Tray.SetDot(color)` (a CSS colour; `""` removes it) shows a dot 5 points across, its centre 3.5 points in from the image's top and right edges, over the icon: on macOS a round custom `NSBox` (`MyGoTrayDot`, whose `hitTest:` lets clicks through to the status item's button) above the button's image, placed again on every `SetImage`; the template keeps its tint. Other platforms ignore it (`platform.TrayDot` is an optional interface; the fake backend records the dot). Docs in docs/menus.md. Test in the patch: `TestTrayDot`; checked on mac-air (light and dark menu bar). |
| `0014-after-waits-while-occluded.patch` | Idle wake-ups (code review 11-02 M2, thread #155): `Context.After` built the view again after its delay whether or not any of the window showed, while animations and `Painter.After` already waited for the window to show again. AudioSmith's clocks and progress (engine busy, a transcription running, playback, the recorder) went on building the whole page twice a second or more with the window closed to the menu bar, minimized or covered. While the window is occluded the frame After asks for now waits, and comes at once when some of the window shows (`SurfaceShown`); changes of the state (`Window.Update`) still build frames as before. Linux and Windows backends have no occlusion and are unchanged. `Tester.SetOccluded` hides and shows a Tester's window. Tests in the patch: `TestAfterWaitsWhileOccluded`, `TestShownWithoutAfter`; AudioSmith's `TestNoTimedBuildsWhileHidden`. |

Make a patch: copy the module (`go env GOMODCACHE`/github.com/egoist/mygo@VERSION) somewhere writable, `git init` and commit it, change it, run its tests on the Mac and Linux, `git diff > third_party/mygo-patches/000N-name.patch`, then run `scripts/vendor-mygo.sh`. A patch may change MyGo's docs too, as sent upstream: the script leaves them out when it applies it.
